name: norvel
author: music-rhythm-and-dance agent
description:
norvel v4 (direction: music, rhythm and dance) - A DRUM GRID: THE SNARE HIT NOBODY IS HOLDING
SKIDS LATE. PRIVATE; never shown to players. Earlier versions: norvel.v1/v2/v3.json.

WHY v4. v3 was too_hard: 7 % over seven Opus players without a demo, 0 % for the one who had one,
and NOBODY EVER SPENT A DEMO ON IT. Its clue was a kick row plus an EMPTY snare row and "n = 3",
so the answer's shape ("fill in the snare row") was obvious and no team wasted a demo on it - but
n was a FREE PARAMETER, so no hypothesis could be tested offline and every one cost a slice of a
round. The picture-pool players said it in their own words: kelmar1a left "basten/tovel/norvel"
undemoed because "the answer shape is obvious", then scored 54/459 on norvel with "for n=2 the
snare is the kick rotated n steps"; kelmar1b coded "the snare copies each kick group placed at the
floor midpoint between consecutive kick group starts", also n=2 only. The classes that worked in
the same run (fennick 11 %/100 %, durnel 100 %, kelmar 100 %) all carry a CHECKSUM CAPTION that
counts the edits ("3 fall", "2 turn", "2 lean"), which lets a rule be falsified offline against
~70 harvested clues without spending a round.

v4 rebuilds the class in that shape (sim/DESIGN_LOOP.md "The checksum caption"):

CLUE = A FINISHED DRUM GRID, four lines. Everything the rule needs is already drawn:

    hat   |x..x|xx.x|.x.x|.xxx|.x.x|x.xx|
    snare |.x..|x...|x.x.|x.x.|..x.|x.x.|
    kick  |x.x.|.x.x|x.xx|.x.x|....|.x..|
    3 slip

Three drum rows over 6-8 bars of four steps ("x" a hit, "." a rest) and a caption that names the
verb and counts the edits.

SOLUTION = the same picture with the snare row edited (seed 227, a typical demo):

    hat   |x..x|xx.x|.x.x|.xxx|.x.x|x.xx|
    snare |.--x|x...|x.x.|-xx.|..-x|x.x.|
    kick  |x.x.|.x.x|x.xx|.x.x|....|.x..|
    3 slip

THE RULE (one clause). A snare hit with NO HAT ABOVE IT AND NO KICK UNDER IT - a step where the
snare is left playing on its own - skids late: it is drawn "-" where it stood, "-" on across the
hat's gap, and lands "x" on the first step where the hat is ticking again. Nothing else changes.
Kid sentence from one demo: "when the hat stops ticking and the kick isn't there either, the
snare hit has nothing to hold it, so it skids along until the hat catches it."
In the demo above the hit at step 1 skids two steps (the hat is off at 1 and 2, back at 3), the
hit at 12 skids one, the hit at 18 skids one; the hits at 8 and 10 sit under hat holes too but a
kick is under them, so they stay put, and the hits at 4, 14, 20, 22 have the hat above them.

WHAT THE CAPTION BUYS (the point of v4). "3 slip" is a checksum on the answer, so a hypothesis
about WHICH hits move can be tested offline against every harvested clue. Measured over a family
of 30 "which snare hits are edited" rules: after 10 harvested clues 1.02 of them still match the
caption on every clue, after 30 clues exactly 1.00 - the true one. A demo alone leaves 5.7 rules
alive (2.6 after two, 1.7 after three). So the SELECTION is findable without spending a round;
what needs the demo is HOW an edit is drawn, which no count can reveal.

WHY THE DRAWING NEEDS THE DEMO. The eight natural renderings of "that hit moves late" - move it
one step, ghost it and move it one step, keep it and add a hit after, change its glyph in place,
move it past the hat's gap without ghosts, keep it and copy it past the gap, skid it the other
way - all score 11.7-21.2 % (i.e. they bank the ~12 % of clues that say "0 slip" and nothing
else). The distance is not constant either: every clue with n >= 2 contains one skid of one step
AND one of two steps, so "it moves one step later" is contradicted inside the demo picture.
This is the fennick shape: the picture shows WHAT changes, the demo shows HOW.

CONSTRUCTION (generate). B = 6-8 bars; 7-10 snare hits, never two adjacent and never on the last
step; 2-4 of them over a kick; 4-9 further kicks; the hat plays every step except ~25 % holes, at
most 2 per bar. n is drawn 0(12 %)/1(10 %)/2(29 %)/3(29 %)/4(20 %) BEFORE any retry, so the
distribution is exact. Every clue plants the near-misses that make one demo enough:
  * >= 2 snare hits with the hat still ticking and no kick under them (they stay)
  * >= 2 snare hits under a hat hole but with a kick under them      (they stay)
  * >= 1 hat hole over a kick alone and >= 2 over empty steps        (nothing happens)
  * n >= 2: one skid of one step and one of two steps; one skid lands on a kick and one lands on
    an empty step (so "it only skids when the way is clear" and its mirror die on the caption)
and n is refused whenever it equals a count a player could read straight off the picture (snare
hits, kicks, hat holes, snare hits over a kick, snare hits with no hat, kicks with no hat, holes
with no snare, bars, ...) so the caption cannot be explained by anything but the rule.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (a) from the clue alone: a drum grid, the answer is this picture with
the snare row edited, and "3 slip" says three edits - a demo-less player echoes the clue and banks
the 12 % of clues that say "0 slip"; (b) harvest ~30 clues and find the one predicate whose count
is always the caption: the snare hits standing alone in their column; (c) the demo shows what an
edit looks like: a dash where the hit stood, dashes across the hat's gap, the hit landing on the
next hat tick; (d) both skid lengths are in the same picture, so the "until the hat catches it"
reading is forced rather than "one step later".

WITNESS TABLE (3000 fresh clues)
  the true rule (solve)                                                     100.00 %
  clue echoed unchanged (the foothold: the "0 slip" clues)                   11.70 %
  RIGHT RULE, WRONG DRAWING (a player without the demo):
    hit moves one step later, no ghost                                       11.70 %
    ghost + hit one step later                                               21.23 %
    hit stays, a copy one step later / glyph change in place                 11.70 %
    moves past the hat's gap without ghosts / stays + copy past the gap      11.70 %
    ghosts but skidding EARLIER                                              11.70 %
  WRONG RULE, RIGHT DRAWING (a player with the demo):
    every snare hit with no hat above it                                      0.00 %
    every snare hit with no kick under it                                     0.00 %
    every snare hit over a kick / every snare hit                             0.00 %
    the same rule applied to the kick row                                     0.00 %
    the n leftmost snare hits                                                13.10 %
    n random snare hits chosen from those with no hat above                  24.40 %
    lone hits but only when no kick lands on the landing step                31.60 %
    lone hits but only when the hat is off on the next step too              11.70 %
  demo replay / empty / junk / unicode / 4000 chars / snare row alone /
    rows swapped / the snare row shifted one step                             0.00 %
  leniency (all 100 %): bare rows with no bars and no labels, other labels, a "|1234|"
    beat header, blank lines, CRLF, tabs, prose around the picture, spaces around the
    bar lines, the caption line kept OR dropped (house rule, 2026-09-05)
  strictness (all 0 %): rows swapped, two rows, four rows, one row, the snare row shifted,
    ghosts turned into rests, ghosts turned into hits, all on one line, one wrong hat cell
Gradient: 0 % (well-formed but the wrong hits) -> 12 % (the format and the "0 slip" clues) ->
21-32 % (the right hits, the drawing or a spurious extra condition wrong) -> 100 % (the rule).

FAIRNESS. One demo plus the caption is enough: the caption alone isolates the edit-set rule
inside a 30-rule family after ~10 harvested clues, and the demo picture contains both skid
lengths plus four kinds of near-miss, so nothing about the drawing has to be guessed twice.

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200: OK, no warnings. score 335/512, solve 468/5000, generate
2833/50000; clue <= 150 chars, solution <= 150. generate deterministic, 0.22 ms mean over 20 000
seeds (p99 1.1 ms, 0 fallbacks); solve 0.003 ms and scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh clues; score
0.023 ms (worst 6 ms on a 4000-char junk answer). Scorer: 0 raises, 0 non-binary results and 0
false positives on 12 000 junk strings; 0 disagreements with an independent re-implementation on
12 000 mutated answers.

LEVERS. Too easy (a player cracks it without a demo): drop the ghost dashes across the gap so the
drawing is a single "-" and an "x" (less to see in one look); make the hat hole above a skidding
hit sometimes three steps wide; stop printing the caption on 1 clue in 4. Too hard (a demo-holder
stays under 30 %): let the skid always be one step; guarantee two lone hits in the same bar; put
two worked skids in a picture with only five snare hits.
generate:
# THE PICTURE: three drum rows over B bars of four steps (hat on top, then snare, then
# kick) and a caption "<n> slip".  THE RULE (one clause): a snare hit with no hat above
# it and no kick under it -- a step where the snare is left playing on its own -- skids
# late: it is drawn "-" where it stood, "-" on across the hat's gap, and lands "x" on
# the first step where the hat is ticking again.  n counts the skidding hits and is 0
# in ~12 % of clues, where the echoed clue scores.
# Every clue plants the near-misses that make ONE demo enough:
#   * >= 2 snare hits with the hat still ticking and no kick under (stay put)
#   * >= 2 snare hits under a hat hole but with a kick under them (they stay)
#   * >= 1 hat hole over a kick alone, >= 2 over empty steps       (nothing happens)
#   * when n >= 2, ONE skid of two steps and ONE of a single step, so no constant
#     distance renders the answer and the demo shows the hat catching the hit
#   * when n >= 2, one skid lands on a kick and one lands on an empty step
FB = ("hat   |xxxx|xxxx|xxxx|.x.x|..x.|x.xx|x..x|\n"
      "snare |x...|x..x|.x..|.x..|x...|.x.x|.x..|\n"
      "kick  |..x.|.x.x|.xxx|...x|.xxx|x..x|.x..|\n"
      "2 slip")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    n = 0 if r.random() < 0.12 else r.choice((1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4))
    for _ in range(300):
        B = r.randint(max(6, n + 3), 8)
        L = 4 * B
        m = r.randint(max(7, n + 5), 10)                 # snare hits, never adjacent
        S = sorted(r.sample(range(L - m), m))
        S = [p + i for i, p in enumerate(S)]             # gaps >= 2, last step free
        Ss = set(S)
        uu = [v for v in range(2, min(4, m - n - 2) + 1) if v != n]
        if not uu:
            continue
        both = r.sample(S, r.choice(uu))                 # snare hits over a kick
        rest = [i for i in range(L) if i not in Ss and i != L - 1]
        K = set(both) | set(r.sample(rest, r.randint(4, 9)))
        cand = [i for i in S if i not in K]              # could be left playing alone
        r.shuffle(cand); r.shuffle(both); r.shuffle(rest)
        cnt = [0] * B                                    # hat holes per bar: at most 2
        A = []
        for a in cand:                                   # the hits that skid
            if len(A) < n and not cnt[a // 4]:
                A.append(a)
                cnt[a // 4] = 1
        if len(A) < n:
            continue
        # a two-step skid: the hat is missing over the next step as well.  With n >= 2
        # the clue always shows one skid of each length.
        el = [a for a in A if a + 2 not in Ss and a + 2 < L and cnt[(a + 1) // 4] < 2]
        if n > 1 and not el:
            continue
        must = el[0] if n > 1 else -1
        never = [a for a in A if a != must][0] if n > 1 else -1
        ext = set()
        for a in el:
            if a != never and (a == must or r.random() < .5) and cnt[(a + 1) // 4] < 2:
                ext.add(a + 1)
                cnt[(a + 1) // 4] += 1
        keep = {a + 1 for a in A} | {a + 2 for a in A}   # the hat must come back here
        holes = set(A) | ext
        free = [i for i in rest if i not in keep]

        def add(pool, k):
            got = 0
            for i in pool:
                if got < k and cnt[i // 4] < 2:
                    holes.add(i)
                    cnt[i // 4] += 1
                    got += 1
            return got

        if not (add([i for i in both if i not in keep], 2) > 1  # over kicked snare hits
                and add([i for i in free if i in K], 1)         # over a kick on its own
                and add([i for i in free if i not in K], 2 + (r.random() < .5)) > 1):
            continue
        land = [a + 2 if a + 1 in ext else a + 1 for a in A]
        if n > 1 and len({j in K for j in land}) < 2:
            continue                                     # one lands on a kick, one free
        # counts a player could read off the picture instead of finding the rule
        if n and n in (m, len(K), len(holes), len(both), len(cand), B, len(ext),
                       len([i for i in S if i in holes]),
                       len([i for i in K if i in holes]),
                       len([i for i in holes if i not in Ss]),
                       len([i for i in S if i not in holes and i not in K])):
            continue
        row = lambda p: "|" + "|".join(
            "".join("x" if 4 * b + j in p else "." for j in range(4))
            for b in range(B)) + "|"
        return ("hat   " + row(set(range(L)) - holes) + "\n" + "snare " + row(Ss)
                + "\n" + "kick  " + row(K) + "\n" + str(n) + " slip")
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    H, S, K, T = clue.split("\n")
    E = list(S)
    for i, q in enumerate(S):
        if q == "x" and H[i] == "." and K[i] == ".":
            j = i
            E[i] = "-"
            while H[j] == ".":                # skid on across the hat's gap
                j += 1 + (S[j + 1] == "|")
                E[j] = "-"
            E[j] = "x"                        # land where the hat ticks again
    return H + "\n" + "".join(E) + "\n" + K + "\n" + T
